To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
heparin of Mr 32 000 has a greater ability to enhance the rate of factor Xa inhibition by antithrombin than does heparin of lower Mr.

1) heparin fractions that bind antithrombin with high affinity, accelerate the inhibition of factor-Xa by antithrombin, 2) the relative molecular mass of heparin influences the rate of inhibition of factor X by antithromb in, and 3) this effect of molecular mass is abolished by 0.3 m-NaCl.
the kinetics of the inhibition of factor IXa (Xa) by antithrombin (AT) are accelerated by heparin and that the relative molecular mass of the heparins used affects the rate of inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of heparin-catalysed antithrombin activity.
the mechanism of the inhibition of factor IXa (FXa) by heparin and antithrombins (AT) and with the effect of heparins of different molecular mass (M(r)) on the inhibition of FXa by AT.
the development of a new generation of antithrombotic agents which have the potential to reduce the risk of haemorrhage associated with heparin treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the rate of inhibition of factor X by antithrombin in the presence of a given concentration of heparin is dependent on the Mr of the heparan sulfate, the concentration of NaCl and the concentration of factor Xa.
the heparin fraction of higher molecular mass (Mr 22,500 and Mr 32.000) had the maximum rate of inhibition, which was due to the involvement of heparins binding to both factor Xa and AT III.
the rate of heparin-catalyzed inhibition of factor X by antithrombin is dependent on both the heparin and the substrate concentrations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pentasacchride is a potent anti-Xa agent but the heparin molecule has a much greater anti-Xa potency.
the heparin-catalysed inhibition of factor X by antithrombin involves the interaction of heparin with both factor Xa and the heparin-antithrombin complex.
heparin catalyses the reaction of antithrombin with factor Xa by binding to both proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anti-factor XA properties of heparins are not solely due to their ability to bind to antithrombins.
the relative molecular mass of heparin is an important factor in determining the anti-factor XA properties of heparins.
the relative molecular mass of heparin is an important determinant of the rate of inhibition of factor X by antithrombin.
